rationale: Every row here is one of the three defects the F5 differential found in the analyzer, plus the oracle defects that had to be fixed alongside them so the differential could see the first two at all. None of the three was visible to a corpus-wide count: in each case the counts stayed healthy while a whole class of output was missing or wrong. (1) CONSTRUCTORS: `Public Sub New()` has no `name` field — the grammar lexes `New` as an anonymous token — so the 'declaration without a name' guard returned before the naming contract was reached and the index contained zero constructors across 435 files. (2) NESTED TYPE CONTAINMENT: a nested enum recorded `owner=Box` on its symbol but no visitor emitted the edge, so containment navigation stopped at the enclosing class. (3) A FIELD'S UNIT IS THE DECLARATOR: `Public Left, Top, Depth As Integer` is one `field_declaration` with three `variable_declarator` children, so it is three members, not one. (4) A CONSTRUCTION WITH ARGUMENTS WAS INVISIBLE ON THE NODE TYPE THE ANALYZER KEYED ON: `New Box(1, 2)` is an `array_creation_expression` with a `type` field, not an `invocation_expression`, so keying on one node type dropped every such construct — 15,577 of them across 1,718 corpus files. The construct was the finding; the LABEL this row first carried (`calls Build -> Box`) was superseded later, because a construction is one syntactic event published as `instantiates` and publishing `calls` beside it counts it twice and puts a constructor in the call graph. Line numbers are MEASURED from this committed file. (5) MEMBER-LEVEL HERITAGE WAS NEVER COLLECTED: `visitHeritage` was called from exactly one place, the TYPE visitor, so `Public Sub Draw() Implements IShape.Draw` published nothing at all. The full-corpus sweep found it as 17 of 23 missing rows, and every one of them read as a self-edge (`implements Initialize -> Initialize`) because a member that implements `IThing.Refresh` is NAMED `Refresh` -- so the oracle was right that a relationship existed and wrong about its shape. (6) THE CENSUS FOUND TWO MORE WHOLE KINDS. A node-type census over 2,660 files showed 146 distinct named types against 42 classified, so the claim that every construct is accounted for was 29% true and nothing had ever measured it. Two gaps fell out: an INTERFACE's members produced nothing (three node types in neither set, so nothing visited them and every interface in an interface-driven codebase was an empty shell), and OPERATORS produced nothing (no name field, plus a visitor that classified the operator's own symbol as punctuation). The census now classifies 145/145 and fails when a node type appears that the analyzer has not accounted for. (7) THE MODIFIER READ WAS A SINGULAR READ OF A REPEATED FIELD. The grammar emits `modifiers` once per modifier, and `childForFieldName` returns one node, so every modifier after the first was invisible: `Public Shared` reported isStatic=false, `Public Overrides` published no overrides edge at all (0 across 435 files), and `Const`, `MustOverride`, `ReadOnly` and `NotInheritable` were missed the same way. VB writes `Public` first by convention, so the one modifier that was ever read was the one least worth reading. The `overrides` edge it unlocked is now qualified by the base type (`Go -> Base.Go`) rather than being a self-edge. (8) THE MODIFIER READ WAS A SINGULAR READ OF A REPEATED FIELD, and it is the largest single defect this wave found. The grammar emits `modifiers` once per modifier, so `Public Overrides Sub` is `modifiers: (...) modifiers: (...)` and `childForFieldName("modifiers")` returned only `public`. Every modifier-dependent fact was therefore wrong wherever the modifier was not written FIRST: `Public Shared` reported isStatic=false, `Public Overrides` published ZERO overrides edges across 435 files and zero on a textbook override, and `Const`, `MustOverride`, `ReadOnly` and `NotInheritable` were missed the same way. VB writes `Public` first by convention, so the one modifier that was ever read was the one least worth reading. It was found because the docs claimed `overrides` was published and it was not -- a false claim in our own documentation, which is the only kind that reliably gets checked. (9) AUDITING `references` -- the label that was 37% of the index and agreed with by NO second implementation, because it had been excluded from the audit on the grounds that the oracle did not derive it. Excluding the largest class did not shrink it; it made it invisible. The oracle now derives it from a declaration's signature `as_clause`s, and that audit immediately found the analyzer reading an `array_type` declared_type as its own text, publishing a `references` target of `Timers.Timer()`. It also found the ORACLE over-deriving 35 rows by walking a declaration's BODY for `as_clause` nodes, so every `Dim x As Pokemon` local became a type reference from the enclosing method — locals are not project-symbol-table members, and the fix is to stop walking at the signature. The #910 lesson cuts both ways: an underived label is a manufactured green, and a label derived wrongly is a manufactured red. Both were live in the same audit.

knownResidual: The namespace symbol is published as `Shapes`, not `Contoso.Shapes`, because the naming contract descends a qualified name to its last segment — the same last-segment rule that makes `Inherits System.Windows.Forms.Form` a single edge to `Form`. `Contoso` is therefore not a symbol, and containment from a dotted namespace starts at its last segment. This is a deliberate, documented contract rather than a defect, and it is the one place where the namespace's full identity is not recoverable from the symbol table alone. Separately, the `Imports` target follows the same rule: `Imports System.Collections.Generic` publishes `Generic`, not the full dotted namespace.
